svg.title: VLANs and 802.1Q trunks: many networks on one set of switches
svg.desc: VLAN = a separate broadcast domain. Access ports carry one VLAN untagged; trunk ports carry many VLANs with a tag
svg.text: VLANs and 802.1Q trunks: many networks on one set of switches
VLAN = a separate broadcast domain. Access ports carry one VLAN untagged; trunk ports carry many VLANs with a tag
PC-A reaches PC-C over the trunk
PC-A to PC-B must be routed
one sub-interface per VLAN = its gateway
THE 802.1Q TAG · 4 BYTES INSERTED INTO THE ETHERNET HEADER ON TRUNKS
VLAN = broadcast domain = (normally) one subnet. Trunk carries them all; the tag says which VLAN each frame belongs to.
Traffic between VLANs MUST be routed (router-on-a-stick or Layer 3 switch). ACLs on that router become the policy point.
